1. Who we are, and what this covers

Atüned is a self report instrument. You write a story or answer questions. The engine reads where charge sits in what you gave it. The app shows you the result.

This policy covers the app at atuned.world/atuned.html, the pages on atuned.world, your account and your billing. It does not cover sites we link to. Each of those has its own policy. The Terms are the other half of the agreement between you and us.

Tula Unified LLC ("we") makes Atüned. Address: 1634 West 39th Place, Los Angeles, California 90062, United States. [CHECK: confirm this is the address to print in public. If it is a home address, a mailing address or a registered agent's address keeps it private.]

Contact, for privacy and for everything else: hello@atuned.world. We have no separate privacy address. [CHECK: confirm hello@atuned.world receives mail and that a person reads it. It is the sender address in the server's settings, which does not prove it receives.]

We are the controller of your data. That means we decide why it is held and how it is used.

People use Atüned from everywhere, and this policy is written for all of them. Section 13 adds what the law gives you in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom. Section 14 adds California. Section 15 points to a separate page for Washington and Nevada.

2. What Atüned is not

Atüned is not medical care. It does not diagnose. It cannot see a disease, an injury or a deficiency, and it is not looking for one. It reads what you typed and what you answered, and nothing else.

It is not therapy. It does not replace a doctor, a therapist or a prescription. Nothing in it is medical advice. It has not been reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration, and no reading has been tested in a clinical trial.

Decisions about your health belong with a licensed professional. If you are under care, stay under it.

It is not an emergency service. We do not read what you write as you write it, so nobody will know you are in danger. If you are not safe, call or text 988 in the United States, or use your local emergency number.

3. What stays on your device

Everything you enter is written to your browser's storage, on your device. Browser storage is a small file store the browser keeps for one website. We do not use cookies.

It holds:

  • the name, sex, date, time and place of birth you enter
  • your answers
  • your stories, exactly as you typed them
  • the imprints the engine read out of your stories
  • the snapshots of your field
  • the avatar and purpose you set
  • your plan, as a word. Never a card.

The name, sex, date, time and place of birth never leave your device. They are not sent when you create an account, and they are not in the copy we hold.

When you are signed in it also holds a sign in token. The token sits under its own key, apart from your record, so an export file never carries it.

If you clear site data or lose the device, that record is gone. The exceptions are a file you exported, and the copy on our server once you have an account (section 4). The copy on our server does not hold your birth details, so a restored record needs them typed in again.

The free quiz keeps your answers in your browser so you can stop and come back. A story typed into the quiz is held in memory only. It is never saved. Close the page and it is gone. The quiz makes no network request.

The app and the pages load no ads, no analytics tags, no tracking pixels, no outside fonts and no outside scripts. The Analytics page in the app is drawn on your device from your own snapshots. Nothing about how you use the app is reported to us. [CHECK: confirm this is still true on the day the page goes live. If an analytics tool is ever added, change this section first.]

Once your record is on our server it is stored scrambled. Each record body is locked with a standard, widely used lock before it is written to our database. The key is held outside the database. 6. What we use it for

We use your data to:

  • run the reading you asked for
  • open your account and keep your record recoverable
  • take payment and keep your plan right
  • send the messages you asked for, such as a reset link or the morning note
  • keep the service secure and limit abuse
  • fix faults
  • meet legal duties, such as tax records

We use it for nothing else. We do not use it to train or refine any model.

The reason the law lets us do each of these is one of four. You asked for it and we need it to deliver (contract). You said yes (consent). It keeps the service safe and working (legitimate interest). The law requires it (legal duty). Section 13 sets out which reason covers which use, for people in Europe and the United Kingdom.

What you write about your body and your mind is health information in many places. We treat all of it that way. We collect it only to run the reading you asked for. We ask before we collect it. We never sell it. Section 15 covers Washington and Nevada.

We do not sell your personal data. We do not share it for advertising. We run no advertising or tracking tools.

8. Delete, export and correct

Delete the record on this device. Settings, Privacy, Delete this record. It is gone from this browser at once. There is no copy unless you made one. It cannot be undone.

Delete your account. Settings, Privacy, Delete account. This deletes your account, the copy of your record on our server, your recovery email, your consent settings, your sign in tokens, your push addresses and your error reports. It leaves our live system at once. A locked copy stays in our backups for 90 days, so you can ask for it back (section 9). Nothing uses that copy for any other purpose. After 90 days it is overwritten. We cannot take one account out of a backup. [CHECK: confirm with the host that a backup cannot be searched, opened or used except to restore, and that it is overwritten on schedule.] Stripe keeps the billing records the law requires. Deleting the account does not delete the record on your device until you do that too. [CHECK: the in-app Delete account control is not built. The server route exists. Until the control ships, deletion is by email to the address in section 19.]

Export. Settings, Privacy. Export this record gives you your device record as a file. Export account data gives you everything we hold under your account as one file. [CHECK: the in-app Export account data control is not built. The server route exists.]

Correct. Change anything you entered, in the app. If an account detail is wrong, such as your recovery email, write to us.

We answer a written request within 30 days. [PROPOSED: 30 days. Europe and the United Kingdom allow one month. California allows 45 days. 30 meets all three. A lawyer confirms.]

Cancelling a paid plan does not delete anything. Your record stays and your plan drops to free.

9. Getting back a deleted account

If you delete your account and want it back, you have 90 days. In that time we can restore the account and your record from backup. These are the steps.

  1. Write to hello@atuned.world within 90 days of the day you deleted the account. Write from the recovery email on the account, if you gave one, and say your username. If you gave none, or you no longer control it, say so and prove the account is yours. [PLACEHOLDER: what proof we accept when the person has lost the account's email. The draft recommends a Stripe receipt in the account's name, plus the date of the account.]
  2. We check that the request comes from the person the account belongs to. We will not restore an account for anyone else.
  3. We restore the account and the record from backup, and tell you by email. [PLACEHOLDER: how long we take. The draft recommends five working days.]
  4. You sign in, or use Forgot your passphrase to set a new one.

Three things to know. The restored record is the one in the last backup before you deleted it. [CHECK: how often backups run, and so how much a person could lose.] Your birth details were never sent to us, so they come back only from your device. If that record is gone too, type them in again. Billing does not come back: your plan returns as free, and you choose again if you want a paid one.

After 90 days the backup is gone. We cannot restore it and nobody can. You can open a new account at any time.

10. Moving data between countries

Our server and database are in the United States. If you use Atüned from another country, your data is sent to the United States when you create an account or sign in. Laws there differ from the laws where you live.

For people in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, the United States is not a country those places have ruled to have the same level of protection for every company. So we need a safeguard. [CHECK: the safeguard is for a lawyer to choose. The likely choice is the standard contractual clauses, which are a set of promises approved by the European Commission that bind the company receiving the data, with the United Kingdom's addendum added for the United Kingdom. The other route is the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, which needs the company to certify itself. Name the choice here once it is made.]

You can ask us for a copy of the safeguard in force. Write to the address in section 19.

Atüned is for people aged [PLACEHOLDER: age floor. Proposed: 18] and over. It is not directed at children. We do not knowingly keep an account for anyone under that age. If we learn that we do, we delete it. If you think a child has an account, write to the address in section 19.

[CHECK: the sign up asks the person to confirm their age with a ticked box, so the floor is more than a line in the terms. At 18 no country's rule on a parent's consent for a child is reached. Those ages run from 13 to 16 across the European Union and are 13 in the United Kingdom.]

12. Your rights, wherever you live

Wherever you live, you may ask us to tell you what we hold about you, correct it, delete it, or give it to you as a file. You may take back a consent you gave, at any time, and taking it back does not undo what was done before. We do not sell your data, so there is nothing to opt out of. We will not treat you worse for using a right.

To use a right, use the controls in section 8 or write to the address in section 19.

If you live in the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom, read section 13. If you live in California, read section 14. If you live in Washington or Nevada, read section 15. Those laws give you the same rights and some more.

This section applies under the California Consumer Privacy Act as changed by the California Privacy Rights Act (CCPA). [CHECK: the law applies to a business above a revenue or volume threshold. We may be below it. We give you these rights either way. A lawyer confirms.]

What we collected in the last 12 months, and why.

  • Identifiers: your username, your recovery email if you gave one, and your IP address. To run your account and keep it secure.
  • Commercial information: your plan and your billing status. To keep your plan right.
  • Sensitive personal information: your stories, answers and readings, which describe your mind and your body, and your account login. To give you the reading you asked for and keep your record recoverable. We use it for nothing else.

What we sold or shared. Nothing. We have sold no personal information. We have shared none for advertising. Sharing here means passing data to a company to show you ads based on what you do across sites. We run no such tools.

16. Security

  • Everything between your device and our server travels over an encrypted connection.
  • We never store your passphrase. We store a slow one way scramble of it, with a different random value mixed into each account's scramble. Nobody can turn it back into the passphrase.
  • Sign in tokens are stored scrambled too. The token itself is never kept.
  • Ten failed sign ins lock a username or a connection for fifteen minutes.
  • Reset links work once and expire in one hour. Using one signs out every device.
  • Stored record bodies are locked as described in section 4.

No system is perfect. If you think your account is at risk, change your passphrase and write to us.

17. If something goes wrong

If we learn that your data was exposed to someone who should not have it, we will tell you by email. We will say what happened, what was exposed and what to do. If the law requires us to tell a regulator, we will. In Europe and the United Kingdom that is within 72 hours of our becoming aware of it, where the risk to people is more than small. We will tell you without delay, and within [PLACEHOLDER: hours or days. The United States health breach rule allows 60 days as the outer limit. Europe asks for no undue delay when the risk to you is high].
